The repo already had one large runtime import cycle (about 110 files, including RoomListStoreV3, SpaceStore and SDKContextClass). This PR adds five files to it: CreateSectionDialog.tsx, its index.ts barrel, CreateSectionDialogViewModel.tsx, tagRoom.ts and getSectionTagForRoom.ts.

Two kinds of import cause this:
1. `section.ts` now imports the new `CreateSectionDialog/index.ts` (line 13) at runtime. That file re-exports `CreateSectionDialog.tsx`, and the dialog imports these at top level:
   - `RoomListStoreV3` (line 19)
   - `SDKContextClass` (line 20)
   - `CreateSectionDialogViewModel` (line 18), which imports `sortRoomsByRecency` (line 21). Through getLastTimestamp → Unread → EventTileFactory → … → InviteDialog, that chain leads back to RoomListStoreV3.

   RoomListStoreV3 imports section.ts (line 42), so the loop closes. The shortest version is dialog → RoomListStoreV3 → section → index → dialog.
2. `section.ts` now imports `tagRoom.ts` (line 18). `tagRoom.ts` already imports `CHATS_TAG`/`isSectionTag` from `section.ts`, so the two files now import each other directly.

What this does at load time: whichever file in the loop loads first, the others can see its exports before they are defined. For example, if RoomListStoreV3 is loading, section.ts may get the dialog module before it has finished running. Or tagRoom.ts may read `CHATS_TAG` from a section.ts that isn't fully loaded yet and get `undefined`. These bugs depend on load order, and the cycle also makes the room-list store harder to load or test on its own.

This removes the section.ts → CreateSectionDialog/index.ts hop that the first three loops share.

Have the dialog stop reaching for singletons. Pass `roomListStore` and `matrixClient` in as props from section.ts, which already has SDKContextClass. CreateSectionDialog.tsx then no longer needs to import RoomListStoreV3 or SDKContextClass at runtime; `import type` is enough for the prop types.

Break the section.ts ↔ tagRoom.ts loop. Move `CHATS_TAG` and `isSectionTag` (and any other constants tagRoom needs) into a small leaf module with no imports, such as `stores/room-list-v3/sectionTags.ts`, that both files import. Another option is to have section.ts call the tag/untag client API directly instead of importing tagRoom.

Check whether CreateSectionDialogViewModel could take already sorted rooms, or a sort function passed in as a prop. Then it wouldn't need a runtime import of sortRoomsByRecency, which leads through getLastTimestamp/Unread into the big existing cycle.

For example, give UnreadFilter a constructor argument or setter like `getCurrentRoomId: () => string | null`, and supply it from RoomListStoreV3 where it builds the filters (getSkipListFilters). RoomListStoreV3 is already in the same cycle group and is what calls `useNewFilters` in the new `updateRoomSkipList()`. With this change, UnreadFilter.ts no longer needs to import SDKContextClass.

The filter stays a pure function of its inputs and needs no context import.

If the filter really must read the store itself, import just the RoomViewStore instance (or a small accessor module that doesn't import SpaceStore) instead of SDKContextClass. Before relying on this, run the rie tools again to confirm the new path doesn't lead back to RoomListStoreV3.

Before this PR, src/flows.ts already led back to the AI tools through existing imports: flows.ts → services/index.ts → services/server.ts → server.ts → app.ts → ai/chat/router.ts → chat.post.ts → chat-request-tool-to-ai-sdk-tool.ts → ai/tools/index.ts → flows/index.ts and operations/index.ts. Your two new imports close that chain into a loop, so position.ts is now one of the files in the cycle. All of these imports run at load time. Depending on which file loads first, position.ts can run while src/flows.ts is only partly evaluated. That is safe only while `getFlowManager` is called inside a function and not at the top level of the module, and every new edge like this makes load order harder to reason about. rie check fails the PR because the cycle grew by one file.

suggestions.text: Remove the top-level import of getFlowManager from position.ts. Inside relayoutFlow, load it lazily only when a reload is needed, e.g. `const { getFlowManager } = await import('../../../flows.js');`. This would remove the position.ts → flows.ts edge, which both loops go through. The tests mock '../../../flows.js', and vi.mock should still apply to dynamic imports.

Have relayoutFlow take the reload as a parameter instead of importing it, for example `relayoutFlow(layoutService, flowsService, flow, onChanged: () => Promise<void>)`, and have callers pass the reload in. This only helps if the callers can get the flow manager without importing src/flows.ts themselves; otherwise the cycle just moves.

Or don't reload the flow engine from position.ts at all. Return whether anything was written (layoutFlow already does) and let the caller decide. OperationsService's own reload path could handle it if the layout writes went through it, but that brings back the per-row reload cost the PR is trying to avoid.
